title: Coherent Control of Channel Dilations Activate Temporal Bell Nonclassicality
authors: H S Karthik, Akshata Shenoy H, A R Usha Devi, Marcin Pawłowski
abstract: The temporal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality witnesses the nonclassicality of temporal correlations, but its violation is generally degraded by environmental noise. Here, we show that violation of the temporal CHSH inequality can be revived through coherent control of noisy quantum evolutions. We compare two physically distinct implementations: coherent control of noisy evolutions induced by interaction of the system with independent environments, and coherent control of two physically distinct, unitarily equivalent Stinespring dilations of the same noisy channel. Although these constructions generate identical deterministic system dynamics, they induce distinctly different post-selected evolutions. With a focus on the amplitude damping channel (ADC), we show that coherent control of equivalent dilations extend the range of temporal CHSH inequality violation well beyond both the incoherently controlled, or deterministic, scenario and what is achievable with independent environments. Under setting-independent post-selection of the coherent control implementation, the resulting violation further certifies that the channel is not strongly CHSH nonlocality-breaking. Our results identify the choice of Stinespring dilation as an operationally relevant resource in coherently controlled tests of temporal quantum correlations.
summary: The paper addresses how environmental noise degrades temporal quantum correlations, measured by the CHSH inequality. It compares two ways to model controlled noise: independent environments versus equivalent Stinespring dilations. The key finding is that coherently controlling the dilation structure allows for a much broader revival of Bell nonclassicality than previously thought possible.
main_problem: The research investigates how coherent control over noisy quantum evolutions can revive the violation of the temporal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality, which is otherwise degraded by environmental noise.
main_result: Coherent control using equivalent Stinespring dilations significantly extends the range of temporal CHSH violation compared to independent environment models or deterministic scenarios. This highlights that the choice of dilation realization is an operationally relevant resource in testing quantum correlations.
method: The authors compare two physical implementations—independent environmental interactions versus unitarily equivalent Stinespring dilations—by calculating the temporal CHSH parameter ($S_T$) using joint probability distributions derived from these controlled evolutions.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is a single qubit undergoing sequential measurements separated by an intermediate dynamical evolution modeled by a quantum channel, specifically focusing on the amplitude-damping channel (ADC). The dynamics are explored via Stinespring dilations and Choi–Jamiołkowski representations.
key_observables: Temporal CHSH parameter ($S_T$), which must exceed 2 to witness nonclassicality; violation of the temporal CHSH inequality.
important_parameters: Noise strength ($\gamma$, related to damping), and the specific choice between independent environments versus equivalent Stinespring dilations.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on assumptions derived from Macrorealism (MR) regarding physical properties existing independently of observation, and non-invasive measurements.
figures_summary: Figures compare temporal CHSH violation vs. damping strength ($\gamma$) for various control methods: Classical Bound, Incoherent Mixture, Environment-Selective Superposition, and Dilation-Selective Superposition, showing the superior activation range of the latter.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem using the temporal CHSH inequality under noise. It then develops mathematical frameworks comparing independent environment models against equivalent Stinespring dilation controls. The core argument is built by calculating $S_T$ for both control types and demonstrating that coherent control at the dilation level yields superior results.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable resource (the choice of dilation) to enhance quantum tests in noisy environments, which is crucial for developing robust protocols in open quantum systems theory relevant to AMO physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of a temporal CHSH inequality experiment using sequential measurements and coherently controlled interaction of the system with independent environments: First, an initial quantum state is measured. Next, the state undergoes noisy evolution resulting from the unitary interaction with independent environments E1 and E2. A control qubit C (acting as the which path qubit) coherently controls the choice of this interaction. After the coherent evolution, the environments are traced out and the branches are coherently recombined (control post-selection and trace out). Finally, the effectively evolved system undergoes a second measurement. Time runs from left to right.

FIG. 2. The temporal CHSH inequality as a function of the damp- ing parameter γ: The red and the blue lines represent the classical bound and the temporal Tsirelson bound (TTB) respectively. The orange curve corresponds to the case where the action of the envi- ronments are incoherently controlled. The purple curve represents the coherent control of the channel implementations using indepen- dent environments. It is observed that the violation of the temporal CHSH inequality is activated beyond the incoherently controlled (or the deterministic) ADC threshold and persists up to γ ≈0.65.

FIG. 3. Schematic of a temporal CHSH inequality experiment using sequential measurements and coherently controlled Stinespring dilations of the noise channel acting on the system : First, an initial quantum state is measured. Following which, the state undergoes noisy evolution resulting from the unitary interaction with an environment E. A control qubit C (acting as the which path qubit) coherently controls the choice of Stinespring dilations. After this coherent evolution, the environment is traced out and the branches are coherently recombined (control post-selection and trace out). Lastly, the effectively evolved system undergoes the second measurement. Time runs from left to right.

FIG. 4. A plot of the variation in the temporal CHSH inequality as a function of γ is shown. The orange curve represents the case when Stinespring dilations are incoherently chosen. The purple curve is due to coherent selection of the unitarily equivalent dilations. Notice that the violation of the temporal CHSH inequality shows activation beyond the ADC threshold and up to γ ≈0.83.

FIG. 5. The temporal CHSH inequality as a function of γ under dif- ferent considerations: (1) The orange curve denotes the case where the choice of the dilation is deterministic or incoherent (classical) mixture, (2) The purple is due to coherent control of the channels with independent environments and (3) The green corresponds to the coherent control of unitary equivalent dilations with the same envi- ronment.
